parts.problem_md:
![Rectangle with a dotted diagonal line marked as 10 cm, a vertical side marked as 6 cm, representing a right triangle within the rectangle.](assets/001-rectangle-with-a-dotted-diagonal-line-marked-as-.png)

The length of the diagonal of the rectangle is 10 cm.

The width of the rectangle is 6 cm.

Work out the area of the rectangle.
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the missing length of the rectangle using Pythagoras in reverse*

$\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}$

**[M1]**

> *Simplify*

$\begin{gathered} = \sqrt{100 - 36} \\ = \sqrt{64} \\ = 8 \text{cm} \end{gathered}$

**[M1]**

> *Find the area of the rectangle by multiplying the length by the width*

$8\times6$

**Final answer:** **48 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>

**[A1]**

parts.problem_md:
Sam has a rectangular pond, $ABCD$.

![q8a-058033-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/002-q8a-058033-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

i) Calculate $BC$.

$BC$ = ...............................m [3]

ii) He puts a fence around the edge of the pond. 
Calculate the length of the fence.

................................m [1]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Find the length of *$BC$* using Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$

$7^{2}+BC^{2}=12^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract *$7^{2}$* from both sides*

$BC^{2}=12^{2}-7^{2}$

> *Take the square root of both sides*

$BC=\sqrt{12^{2}-7^{2}}$

**[1]**

$BC=9.75m$ **[1]**

**Answers between 9.746 and 9.747 will be accepted**

ii) *The length of the fence will be the same as the perimeter of the rectangle* *Add up the lengths of all of the sides of the rectangle*

$7+7+9.75+9.75$

$33.5m$ **[1]**

**Answers between 33.492 and 33.494 or an answer of 33.49 will be accepted**

equations.alt: a squared plus b squared equals c squared
7 squared plus B C squared equals 12 squared
B C squared equals 12 squared minus 7 squared
B C equals square root of 12 squared minus 7 squared end root

$y=\sqrt{5.3^{2}-4.4^{2}}$

**[1]**

$=2.954657341$

> *Round to 3 significant figures*

**2.95**** ****[1]**

** or 2.954 to 2.955**

![q9-058031-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/006-q9-058031-octnov2018-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

The diagram shows a field in the shape of a trapezium. $AB=150m,BC=90m$ and $CD=120m$. 
Angle $ABC$ = angle $BCD$ = $90^{\circ}$.

i) Show that $AD=95m$, correct to the nearest metre.

[3]

ii)A fence is built around the perimeter of the field.

It costs `$ 48` to build each 5-metre section of the fence. Calculate the cost of building this fence.

`$` .................................... [3]
parts.solution_md:
(i)*Draw a triangle **ADX **as shown below* *DX **will be 90 m as it is the same as **CB* *AX **will be 30 m as it is the difference between **DC** and **AB*

![pythagoras-h-3-1](assets/007-pythagoras-h-3-1.png)

> *Apply Pythagoras to the triangle **AXD **to find length **AD*

$AD=\sqrt{30^{2}+90^{2}}=94.86832981...m$

**Method ****[2]**

**Unrounded answer**** [1]**

> *Round to the nearest metre*

**95 m** *This is a "show that" question, so full working needs to be shown  *

(ii) *Find the total perimeter (distance around the edge)* *Use the 95 m value for the length of **AD*

*120 + 90 + 150 + 95 = 455 m*

**[1]**

*It costs \$48 per 5 metres* *So find how many 5 metres are in 455 m*

*455 ÷ 5 = 91 (lots of 5 m)*

**[1]**

> *Find the cost for 91 lots of \$48*

*91 × 48 = \$4368*

**\$4368** **[1]**

C D space equals space 120 space straight m
A D space equals space 95 m
A D equals square root of 30 squared plus 90 squared end root space equals space 94.86832981... space straight m

parts.problem_md:
The length of one side of a rectangle is 12cm.

The length of the diagonal of the rectangle is 13cm.

Calculate the area of the rectangle.

.......................................... cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> *Use Pythagoras' Theorem to find the width of the rectangle.*

![uqhxR9U~_oct-nov-2020-0580-12-q19](assets/008-uqhxr9u-oct-nov-2020-0580-12-q19.gif)

> *We need to find one of the shorter sides of the triangle, so substitute into *$a=\sqrt{c^{2}-b^{2}}$* *

$a = \sqrt{( 13 )^{2} - ( 12 )^{2}} = 5$

* ***[1]**

> *Area of a rectangle = length x width*

> *Multiply the length of the rectangle by the width to find the area of the rectangle. *

$12\times5=60\mathrm{cm}^{2}$

* ***[1]**

$60\mathrm{cm}^{2}$* ***[1]**

equations.alt: a equals square root of c squared minus b squared end root
12 cross times 5 equals 60 space cm squared
bold 60 bold space bold cm to the power of bold 2
